evidence.field: description, source, author, reuse rights, original file link
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies `半-bronze.svg` as a vector depiction of 半 in bronze script. It cites Sinica Database, Chinese Etymology, CUHK and other sources, and identifies image B01144 on the Hanziyuan 半 page as the source for this drawing. The file is marked public domain, with the creator’s SVG representation released for unrestricted use. The page exposes the original image link, but opening that image returned a cache-miss error; the rendered glyph was not inspected.
evidence.title: File:半-bronze.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The exact file page identifies `Shuowen Seal Radical 018.svg` as an uploader-created, manually straightened depiction of a Shuowen Jiezi Lesser Seal form. It gives the uploader as author and CC BY-SA 3.0 as the license, requiring attribution and share-alike for adaptations. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The source page appeared in search results, but a direct page open failed with a cache miss; its pixel shape was not inspected in this research.
evidence.title: File:Shuowen Seal Radical 018.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: 漢字構形資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The record labels a bronze 半 example as 集成04315 and a Small Seal form as 說文. It interprets the upper 八 as division and lower 牛 as the ox divided. These are database labels and an analysis; the page does not itself provide a primary transcription or establish the precise date of that individual graph.
evidence.title: 漢字「半」：字形演變

evidence.text: The entry presents a bronze-form analysis of 半 as 八 plus 牛, assigns 八 both division-related semantic and phonetic roles, and attributes to 何琳儀 the proposal that 半 is an early graph of 判. It proposes ‘split/open’ as an original sense extended to ‘half.’ It also reports variants substituting 斗 or 升 for 牛 and another form substituting 刃 for 斗. The entry does not establish an exact date or complete order for those forms, nor a dated sequence for the proposed semantic extension.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：半

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry quotes the received Shuowen explanation ‘物中分也。从八，从牛。牛為物大，可以分也’ and gives Mandarin bàn. It documents uses for one half, a middle part or point in time or space, very little, and partial or incomplete, with cited examples including Zhuangzi and later works. The cited examples and glosses do not establish a chronological path among these senses.
evidence.title: [A00435] 半 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction dataset; supplied local table
evidence.field: exact local rows for 八 and 半 in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv
evidence.text: The supplied exact Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 八: Mandarin bā, Middle Chinese transcription peat, Old Chinese *pˤret; 半: Mandarin bàn, Middle Chinese transcription panH, Old Chinese *pˤan-s. The Old Chinese forms share an initial but have different endings. This is compatible with a possible sound relation but does not establish the proposed phonetic role of 八. The dataset PDF was found in search results, but opening it returned HTTP 502; these values are attributed to the supplied local rows, not to an opened PDF.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.field: kMandarin; sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt exact rows 八, 半, 牛
evidence.text: The supplied rows give current Mandarin readings 八 bā, 半 bàn, and 牛 niú. These are modern metadata, not evidence for ancient sound relationships or graphic analysis. The exact official Unicode per-character lookup URLs were attempted but could not be opened, so the rows are supported here by the supplied local table only.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup for 八 (also attempted U+534A 半 and U+725B 牛)

evidence.text: The official Unihan search documentation describes Mandarin readings as searchable character properties. It supports the role of Unihan as a current character-data source, not as evidence of ancient pronunciation or a historical component role.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Search Page

search_audit.outcome: Search exposed the exact file description: uploader-made, manually straightened Shuowen Lesser Seal redraw with CC BY-SA 3.0. The exact page later failed direct opening with a cache miss.

search_audit.query: 半 小篆 金文 集成04315 CUHK 半 字形演變 牛 八 半-bronze.svg Commons
search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK and Academia Sinica character records and the Commons bronze file page. The Commons page identifies the character, source image B01144 and public-domain dedication. The original SVG link returned a cache-miss error, preventing visual inspection.

search_audit.query: Unihan 半 U+534A kMandarin bàn Unicode; Baxter Sagart 2014 八 *pˤret 半 *pˤan-s Old Chinese dataset PDF
search_audit.outcome: The three official Unicode per-character pages could not be opened. The Baxter–Sagart PDF was found in search but failed on open with HTTP 502. Supplied exact local rows were checked and retained with local provenance; Unicode search documentation was opened.
A focused follow-up search did not surface the individual records in accessible form. Per-character URLs had already failed when directly opened.

gaps: The bronze SVG page is well-described and has a direct original link, but the image request returned a cache miss and no local copy exists in the manifest; its rendered pixels and visual suitability could not be checked. No glyph image is selected.

The supplied local seal SVG was inspected as SVG path data, but prior visual review in the dossier found its strokes unsuitable for illustrating the recorded Small Seal form or 八-and-牛 account. The Commons source page describes it as a manually straightened modern redraw; do not label it an artifact image.
No primary transcription or photograph of the cited 集成04315 inscription was inspected, so the specific graph’s reading and date remain dependent on database records.
The proposed ‘split/open’ to ‘half’ semantic development is undated. The available historical glosses and examples do not establish when the senses arose or their links.

The phonetic assignment for 八 is a source analysis. The supplied Baxter–Sagart reconstructions *pˤret and *pˤan-s share an initial but differ in their endings; the PDF could not be opened, and this comparison alone does not establish the role.
The official Unicode kMandarin pages for 八, 半, and 牛 and the Baxter–Sagart PDF were inaccessible in this run. Exact readings are reported from supplied local rows only.

limitations.text: Commons records a bronze-script redraw of 半 and provides source identifier B01144 plus an original SVG link, but that asset request returned a cache miss. Without inspecting the rendered form, this candidate cannot be confidently selected to illustrate the bronze shape or the proposed components.

The Shuowen Lesser Seal redraw is modern and licensed CC BY-SA 3.0, but prior pixel review indicates the supplied local image does not match the recorded Small Seal form closely enough to support its use for this entry.
